decision: Keep multi-file ADRs under docs/adr, with DESIGN, TODO, and open questions as separate logs.
rationale: Chat history drops pivots and rejected options. A single giant decision log does not scale for this catalog, and the filesystem stays the offline source of truth.

rejected.reason: Fine for a tiny repo. This catalog needs multi-file ADRs.
Not reviewable in PRs and not reliable across agents.

rejected.option: GitHub Issues as the sole ADR and TODO store
rejected.reason: Optional mirror later, not the source of truth.

decision: Grok CLI stays the primary operator interface. The bootstrap replays skills and MCP for that CLI.
rationale: The repo goals already name Grok CLI as primary, and the current skills and MCP wiring live there.

rejected.option: Agent-agnostic-only repo with no preferred CLI

rejected.reason: Strong catalog candidates, not where the skills and MCP wiring live.

decision: Track upstream tools by pinned commit. Do not vendor their history into this repo by default.
rationale: Pins stay scriptable and the tree stays small. Subtree embeds are rare and need an explicit checklist.

rejected.reason: Unbounded growth, a poor default for large runtimes.

rejected.option: Floating main only with no pins

rejected.reason: Still noisy for entries operators never edit.

decision: Ship a first-party bootstrap at bootstrap/grok-cli that replays skills and a surgical config merge.
rationale: Operator customizations must replay on a new machine. Do not store secrets in the repo.

rejected.option: Document-only setup with README steps and no scripts
rejected.reason: Drifts and is hard to re-run.

rejected.option: Subtree the whole ponytail or codebase-memory repos
Publish skills only to a separate skills repo

decision: Use the light in-repo process docs and the project-process skill, not a heavy knowledge platform.
rationale: Markdown covers ADR, TODO, and open questions for agents. The catalog stays lean.

rejected.option: Replace the process with adr-tools only
rejected.reason: Numbers files, and misses DESIGN, TODO, and open questions.

rejected.option: Confluence or Linear as the sole ADR and TODO store
log4brains or a full AKM platform

decision: Keep named deployment profiles and an env registry instead of one hard-coded stack.
rationale: Profiles make local, balanced, and max-performance explicit. The registry is what machines check.

rejected.option: A single hard-coded stack in the README only

decision: Keep write-guard as an MCP policy layer and keep agent-cage as the container.
rationale: A shell can bypass MCP, so the container stays required. The YAML policy and audit log match the cage.

rejected.reason: No audit and no secret globs.

rejected.option: Replace the cage with a different sandbox product

rejected.reason: Weaker for network and package installs.

decision: One-shot work writes a definition of done and checks a lab or a waived cage before cloud spend.
rationale: Cheap local iteration comes first. Stop conditions block an infinite loop.

rejected.option: Always ask until the spec is fully written

rejected.reason: Expensive and against the local-first goal.

decision: Port skills by a hybrid rule: first-party where we must enforce the process, path snapshots or docs otherwise.
rationale: A full embed of a large upstream skill tree drifts. Raw gstack install is blocked.

rejected.reason: Huge surface and the wrong default.

decision: Do not use AgenC as the primary operator interface. Grok CLI stays primary and agent-cage stays the lab.
rationale: The AgenC trial failed the daily UX and auth tests. Two primaries would mean two logins and two prompt styles.

rejected.option: AgenC as primary despite the TUI pain

rejected.reason: Two auth surfaces and two TUIs.

rejected.option: Immediate full port of AgenC features

decision: Keep two surfaces. Grok is the monitor and OpenCode plus a local engine is the worker. Do not add a third primary runtime.
rationale: Skills stay one markdown source of truth. A third TUI and daemon repeats the same class of risk as a second primary.

rejected.option: Hermes Agent as a third primary runtime

decision: Expose onboard, stage, and ship. Keep each harness behind a small adapter instead of embedding it.
rationale: The product surface is three verbs. Full harness installers stay out until an adapter is ready.

decision: Optional operator TUIs stay optional. Preference is measured in use, and agent-cage stays the lab.
rationale: A silent edit of the AgenC rejection would erase history. Isolation for a marketplace tool does not replace the cage.

rejected.option: Silent amendment of the AgenC rejection
Making AgenC co-primary or the default

decision: Local inference is a pluggable spine. The host may use more than one engine, and this repo does not vendor an engine.
rationale: One engine name blocks the others. Cluster serving is not the laptop default.

rejected.option: Shimmy as the named X engine
rejected.reason: The owner named a different engine.

rejected.option: llama.cpp direct as the only engine

decision: data/tools.json stays a slim subset. It does not have to mirror every TOOLS.md row.
rationale: A full rewrite of the catalog blocks the launch work. Every JSON name must still appear in TOOLS.md.

rejected.option: Restore JSON until it matches every TOOLS.md row

rejected.reason: Breaks readers that already open it.
Agents treat a count mismatch as a bug.

rationale: A transcript pane would mis-state the product. Confidence is a margin chip, not a correctness percent.

rejected.reason: The product is a decision API.

rejected.reason: The forms model is the default.
